stories.title: India orders evacuations as Cyclone Arnab looms
summary: Indian authorities ordered nearly 100,000 people to evacuate homes in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, ahead of a severe cyclone the national weather office expects to make landfall by Wednesday.

Cyclone Arnab is forecast to hit India’s southwestern Andhra Pradesh coast as a “very severe cyclonic storm”, with gusts of up to 150 kilometres (93 miles) per hour on Wednesday morning, the India Meteorological Department said in a bulletin.
Indian media reported that as many as 50,000 people have been told to move to safe areas in Andhra Pradesh, and 48,000 in Odisha.

stories.title: No pressure from US to cut Russian oil imports, says Indian oil minister
summary: India has faced no pressure from ​the US to reduce its Russian crude ‌imports, oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Tuesday at an industry event. “I never felt anything,” Puri said when ​asked if there has been pressure to ​cut Russian oil imports.
He said India ​was getting 0.2 per cent of its oil imports from Russia before the Ukraine war, while imports have surged since the war ​started due to discounts on Russian oil.

India’s imports ​of Middle Eastern crude oil surged in September, returning to pre-war ‌levels, ⁠while its refiners cut back purchases of Russian oil amid stiff competition from China, ship-tracking data showed.

stories.title: Israel to give verdict on Netanyahu in pivotal election
summary: A deeply divided Israel headed to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023 attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s rightward drift.

The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by a devastating military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank, along with a move towards hard-right religious nationalism.

stories.title: Sudan drone strikes kill 21, cause mass outages in east
summary: Sudan’s warring sides have traded drone strikes that killed 21 people in the western Darfur region and left vast swathes of the country’s east without electricity, medics and witnesses said Tuesday.

A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the de facto capital of Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Darfur, killed 21 people and wounded at least 40 others, a medical source and witnesses told AFP.
The RSF has in turn launched repeated strikes targeting Khartoum’s airport, as well as dams and power stations across the country’s east.

stories.title: Govt asks Sepa to examine Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam project, seeks input on environmental protection
summary: KARACHI: Facing mounting public protests over the ongoing construction at Nehr-i-Khayyam, the provincial government has approached the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency (Sepa) for “examining” the scheme.

Explaining the purpose of the scheme, the local government department stated in the letter that it aimed to rehabilitate the existing Nehr-i-Khayyam and divert sewerage flows to “support improved drainage, reduce contamination and promote a cleaner and healthier environment”.

Says rehabilitation scheme will help wastewater treatment, plantation and public recreation It said that the proposed works include the rehabilitation of around one kilometre of the existing drain, the construction of another kilometre of sewerage line and a multi-cell box drain.

stories.title: Why the world still needs World Trade Organisation
summary: In its World Trade Report 2026 launched last month, the Geneva-based body tells us what would happen if the rules are simply allowed to ‘wear away.’ It says the outcome would be quite expensive for the global economy.
The report is the WTO’s flagship study and looks back over 80 years of trade rules.
The WTO rules restrain discrimination against non-members and shape how free trade agreements are built.

stories.title: At UNGA debate, Pakistan warns against adding more members to Security Council, extending veto privileges
summary: Pakistan has warned that adding more permanent members to the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and extending veto privileges would “deepen existing inequalities, perpetuate historical advantages and increase the risk of Council paralysis”.

He called for a balanced approach combining restrictions on veto use with enhanced representation and a stronger role for elected members of the UNSC, making its decision-making “more democratic and providing an effective check on the exercise of veto power”.

A recent UN report has also warned that the veto power of the five permanent members of the Security Council is one of the reasons multilateral mechanisms have been unable to prevent or stop the growing number of state-based conflicts.

stories.title: Pakistan's last antique restorers give old treasures new life
summary: Antique dealer Ahsan Shakeel polishes an artefact outside his shop selling vintage items in Rawalpindi on October 20, 2026. —AFP Today, he is one of the last master restorers preserving antique metalware in Pakistan.
The shop owner and his colleague Shakeel Ahmed restore the battered items by hammering out dents, re-tinning the interiors over coal fires, and polishing the metal.
Antique dealer Ahsan Shakeel shows an artefact at his shop selling vintage items in Rawalpindi on October 20, 2026. —AFP After restoration, a piece can sell between $100 and $1,000.

stories.title: Jordan strikes militant groups in Syria after church attack
summary: The Jordanian military said it had struck “terrorist organisations” in neighbouring Syria on Monday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a church last week, hours after authorities arrested three men they accused of the killings.
On Friday, gunmen killed nine people during a funeral service at the Greek Orthodox St George’s Church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate, southern Jordan.
Major General Abdullah al-Maaytah, Jordan’s director of public security, on Monday named the three detained suspects as Hazza Zaidan Mohammed, Meshal Zaidan Mohammed and Ahmad Sami Hussein.

stories.title: Makkah pact allies move from defence to diplomacy
summary: The first meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement countries with Tehran reflected the realisation that regional tensions need to be addressed through diplomacy, even as the participating countries strengthen their own defence cooperation.

The discussions took place against a backdrop of heightened concern over the escalating conflict between Yemen’s Ansar Allah rebels against Saudi Arabia, the security of the Strait of Hormuz and the prospect of renewed US and Israeli military action against Iran.

Monday’s meeting offered Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye an opportunity to convey their concerns directly to Iranian leaders, while exploring whether regional cooperation could help contain the risks of a wider conflict.

summary: Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf has identified a technical flaw in Babar Azam’s batting, saying the seasoned batsman’s open right shoulder is affecting his ability to judge the line and movement of deliveries.
